glossary.meaning: To enter. Входит is present tense: she enters.
Into the shop, or inside a parcel. В магазин indicates movement; в моей посылке indicates location.
Shop; here the destination after в.
On or onto. На столе describes location; на стол describes where something is put.
Table. Столе is used for location, стол for movement onto it, and столом after со.
To lie or be resting somewhere. Лежат is plural, referring to the parcels.
Two. Две is the feminine form used with посылки.
White. Белые agrees with the plural parcels.
Parcel. Посылка is singular; посылку is a singular direct object; посылке follows location prepositions. Посылки refers to two parcels or parcels as a direct object.
Hello; a polite greeting.
I, the person speaking.
Here, in this shop or on this parcel.
There is; used to ask whether a parcel or card is available. У вас есть means 'do you have'.
My. Моя agrees with feminine посылка; моей is used with feminine nouns in the other cases shown here.
To ask a question. Спрашивает means 'she asks'.
Yes; confirms what someone says.
Here is; points out the parcel being offered.
Your, addressing someone politely. Ваша agrees with feminine посылка.
To say or speak. Говорит means 'says'.
Salesperson or shopkeeper.
To give. Даёт means 'gives'; the recipient is expressed with Анне or ей.
Large or big. Большую agrees with посылку as a direct object.
To read. Читает means 'she reads'.
Name; here the name written on a parcel.
Whose. Чья is feminine, agreeing with посылка.
This, or 'this is'; used to identify a parcel or a person.
To mix things up. Перепутал is masculine past tense: he mixed up the parcels; the perfective verb presents this as a completed mistake.
To put or set something down. Кладёт means 'she puts'.
To take or pick up. Берёт means 'takes'.
Small. Маленькую agrees with посылку as a direct object.
And or but, introducing a contrast: one parcel has a book, while the other has a cup.
She. Она is the subject; ей means 'to her' when Ivan gives her the parcel.
Thank you.
Book.
For, indicating who the book is intended for; followed by the genitive case.
Sister. Сестры is genitive singular after для and in the birthday construction.
Cup.
To smile. Улыбается means 'she smiles'.
It is good that; introduces something the speaker is pleased about.
I have; literally a possession construction using у and the genitive form меня.
You have, using polite 'you'. Also used in У вас есть to ask whether something is available.
Now, after the parcels have been sorted out.
One's own. Свою means Anna's own parcel and agrees with посылку.
Then or afterwards.
To look at; на introduces what someone looks at.
Card, here a greeting card for a birthday. Открытки is plural; открытка is singular.
Next to. Со is a form of с; столом takes the instrumental case.
My sister has; here it introduces the statement that her birthday is tomorrow.
Tomorrow.
Birthday; a fixed expression literally meaning 'day of birth'.
With; here describing a card featuring a cat. The following noun takes the instrumental case.
Cat. Кошкой is instrumental singular after с.
